0.0.n: This is the name of Japan’s government ministry responsible for legal affairs.

0.1.n: Marks the ministry as the topic of the sentence, which continues into the next line.

0.3.n: Past passive form of 取りまとめる, describing a report that has been put together.

0.4.n: A written document, described here by the preceding verb form.

0.5.n: Part of をもとに, which identifies what serves as the basis for an action.

0.6.n: Here, もと refers to the information used as a foundation for further action.

0.7.n: Completes をもとに, linking the report to the action based on it.

1.0.n: Combines with 防止法 to form the name of the Anti-Prostitution Act.

1.1.n: Combines 防止, prevention, with 法, law; here it forms part of the law’s name.

1.2.n: Links the law to 改正, showing which law would be revised.

1.3.n: Refers to changing the law’s provisions, rather than replacing the entire law.

1.4.n: Marks 改正 as the goal in the expression に向けた.

1.5.n: Past form of 向ける; に向けた describes the following noun by its goal, not necessarily a past action.

1.6.n: Refers to examining and discussing possible changes before deciding what to do.

1.7.n: Marks 検討 as what the ministry will advance.

1.8.n: Describes moving the deliberations forward, not physically moving something.

1.9.n: In ものとみられます, this frames the preceding action as an anticipated development rather than a physical thing.

1.10.n: Marks the preceding statement as the content of the assessment expressed by みられます.

1.11.n: Polite passive form of みる, expressing an assessment rather than literal seeing.

0.lit: As for the Ministry of Justice, with the compiled report as a basis,
0.tip: をもとに means that the following action uses the preceding information as its basis.

1.lit: It is considered that deliberations aimed at revision of the Prostitution Prevention Act will be advanced.
1.tip: ものとみられます is a formal news expression presenting an expected development, not a confirmed decision.
